title: Everything You Need To Know About Sony’s New Super-Telephoto Primes
summary: Sony's 400mm f/4.5 GM & 600mm f/6.3 GM aim to make serious reach more realistic for wildlife photographers – without the bulk.
body_markdown:
Sony has added two new G Master super-telephoto primes to its E-mount lineup: the[FE 400mm f/4.5 GM](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/lenses/prime-lenses/p/sel400f45gmw?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article) and the[600mm f/6.3 GM](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/lenses/prime-lenses/p/sel600f63gmw?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article) . For photographers who spend their time tracking birds, wildlife, sports or distant subjects, their shared proposition is immediately compelling: long focal lengths in unusually portable bodies.


****


Both lenses weigh under 1,000 grams and are compact enough to fit in a smaller camera backpack. That changes the practical equation for photographers who want reach but do not want to carry – or handhold – traditional large-format super-telephotos all day.[Sony Artisan Miguel Quiles](https://alphauniverse.com/member/#/miguel-quiles/) paired the new lenses with his[Alpha 7R VI](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/interchangeable-lens-cameras/full-frame/p/ilce7rm6b?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article) and[Alpha 9 III](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/interchangeable-lens-cameras/all-interchangeable-lens-cameras/p/ilce9m3b?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article) cameras in the[latest video on the Alpha Universe YouTube Channel](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e6G1j_y_sS0) . Check out some of his highlights and photos below.


****


Photo by Miguel Quiles. Alpha 7R VI. 600mm f/6.3 G Master. 1/3200-sec., f/6.3, ISO 4000


****


****


#### The Headline: Compact, Balanced Reach


****


The[400mm f/4.5 G Master](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/lenses/prime-lenses/p/sel400f45gmw?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article) weighs 994 grams, while the[600mm f/6.3 G Master](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/lenses/prime-lenses/p/sel600f63gmw?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article) comes in at 995 grams. The one-gram difference is almost beside the point; the notable part is that Sony has kept both lenses at roughly the same lightweight, travel-friendly threshold despite their distinct focal lengths.


****


Photo by Miguel Quiles. Alpha 7R VI. 400mm f/4.5 G Master. 1/2500-sec., f/4.5, ISO 3200


****


Sony achieves that compact character in part through a single front lens-element design. The result is a more centered weight distribution, which should make the lenses easier to balance and more comfortable to use handheld. Both lenses also focus internally, so their physical length does not change as focus shifts – helping preserve that balance in use.


Photo by Miguel Quiles. Alpha 9 III. 600mm f/6.3 G Master. 1/1250-sec., f/6.3, ISO 250


#### [FE 400mm F4.5 GM OSS](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/lenses/prime-lenses/p/sel400f45gmw?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article) : Fast, Bright & Ready For Action


The[400mm f/4.5 G Master](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/lenses/prime-lenses/p/sel400f45gmw?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article) combines a relatively bright maximum aperture with a compact optical design. It includes 22 elements in 16 groups, an 11-blade circular aperture and three Super ED elements. Two XD linear motors – one assigned to each focus group – drive the lens’ autofocus system.


Photo by Miguel Quiles. Alpha 9 III. 400mm f/4.5 G Master. 1/2000-sec., f/4.5, ISO 400


****


On the exterior, photographers get AF/MF and full-time DMF controls, a focus limiter, Optical SteadyShot controls and mode switches, plus four customizable focus-hold buttons. A customizable function ring can also be assigned to a preferred task – one useful setup is switching quickly between full-frame and APS-C crop modes. For working outdoors, the front element features Nano AR Coating II to help repel water, oil and dust. The lens is also dust- and moisture-resistant, giving it the weather-conscious build expected of a G Master optic.


****


Photo by Miguel Quiles. Alpha 9 III. 400mm f/4.5 G Master. 1/3200-sec., f/4.5, ISO 250


****


#### [FE 600mm F6.3 GM OSS](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/lenses/prime-lenses/p/sel600f63gmw?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article) : More Reach, Nearly The Same Footprint


****


The[600mm f/6.3 G Master](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/lenses/prime-lenses/p/sel600f63gmw?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article) mirrors the 400mm closely in its external layout and control set, making the transition between the two straightforward for photographers who use both. Internally, it uses 24 elements in 17 groups, including one ED element, and shares the same single front lens-element approach.


****


That 600mm focal length is particularly attractive for small or distant subjects, including birds that are difficult to approach. Just as important, its 995-gram weight means photographers can pack meaningful reach without reserving an entire bag – or an entire day’s energy – for one lens.


****


Photo by Miguel Quiles. Alpha 9 III. 600mm f/6.3 G Master. 1/640-sec., f/6.3, ISO 640


####


Teleconverter Compatibility Extends The Range


****


Both lenses are compatible with Sony’s 1.4x and 2.0x teleconverters, giving photographers additional flexibility when the subject demands more magnification. The[400mm](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/lenses/prime-lenses/p/sel400f45gmw?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article) can extend to 560mm at f/6.3 with the 1.4x teleconverter or 800mm at f/9 with the 2.0x teleconverter. The[600mm](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/lenses/prime-lenses/p/sel600f63gmw?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article) becomes an 840mm at f/9 with the 1.4x teleconverter or a 1,200mm at f/13 with the 2.0x teleconverter.


****


#### Field Impressions: Built For Real Wildlife Work


****


In wildlife shooting, portability is not merely a convenience – it can determine whether a lens makes it into the field at all. After using both lenses in Florida’s summer heat and humidity, the reviewer found their low weight and compact size especially welcome, noting how easily they fit into a small camera bag.


****


Photo by Miguel Quiles. Alpha 9 III. 600mm f/6.3 G Master. 1/1000-sec., f/6.3, ISO 800


****


Performance was equally encouraging. Paired with Sony’s[Alpha 9 III](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/interchangeable-lens-cameras/all-interchangeable-lens-cameras/p/ilce9m3b?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article) and[Alpha 7R VI](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/interchangeable-lens-cameras/full-frame/p/ilce7rm6b?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article) cameras, both lenses quickly acquired and tracked stationary and moving subjects, including at up to 120 frames per second. Even when branches sat in the foreground between the camera and a bird, autofocus remained accurate and responsive.


****


Photo by Miguel Quiles. Alpha 7R VI. 600mm f/6.3 G Master. 1/1250-sec., f/6.3, ISO 1600


****


#### A Welcome Shift In Super-Telephoto Primes


Sony’s new[400mm f/4.5 G Master](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/lenses/prime-lenses/p/sel400f45gmw?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article) and[600mm f/6.3 G Master](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/lenses/prime-lenses/p/sel600f63gmw?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article) are not simply new long lenses, they are a focused attempt to make high-end super-telephoto photography more mobile. With sub-1,000-gram weights, internal focusing, weather-conscious construction, extensive physical controls and teleconverter compatibility, each gives wildlife photographers a serious option for traveling light without giving up reach.


****


****


The choice comes down to shooting style. The[400mm f/4.5 GM](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/lenses/prime-lenses/p/sel400f45gmw?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article) offers a brighter aperture and a versatile starting point for action and wildlife. The[600mm f/6.3 GM](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/lenses/prime-lenses/p/sel600f63gmw?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article) prioritizes native reach in an almost identical-size package. Either way, Sony’s newest G Masters point toward a welcome shift: super-telephoto primes that are easier to carry, easier to handhold and better positioned for the moments that happen far from the trailhead.
